When aqueous NaCl is electrolyzed, the following reactions occur: 
°At the cathode (reduction): 2H2O +2e-  → H2 +2OH-
° At the anode (oxidation): 2Cl- → Cl2 + 2e–  
1. Calculate the total charge passed: Q=1 × t=9.65 A × 1000s = 9650C 
2. Calculate the moles of electrons transferred: n = Q / F = 9650C / 96485 C/mol 0.1 mol 
3. Determine the moles of NaOH formed: From the cathode reaction, 2 moles of electrons produce 2 moles of OH ions. Since Na+ ions are already present in the solution, they combine with OH-ions to form NaOH. So, 1 
mole of electrons produces 1 mole of OH-and hence 1 mole of NaOH. 
Moles of NaOH = moles of electrons = 0.1 mol 
4. Calculate the mass of NaOH formed: Mass of NaOH = moles of NaOH molar mass of NaOH Mass of NaOH = 0.1mol × 40g / mol = 4.0g
